date.source: The results page's own title names the day and month ("of April 30th"); no document states the year directly. NOT day-of-week reasoning (CURATION.md's own day-of-week-method caution: brand day is fiction, never contradiction-grade) — the year is read from the fed's own guestbook, whose single earliest-ever entry (27 Apr 1998) opens an unbroken thread of match challenges and roster chatter (the wheelchair-match negotiation, the AEW Top Stable Title program, "Big Sexy" Kevin Nash's callouts) that runs through 7 May 1998 and lands on exactly the same storylines the front page's own "Last Updated= Sunday, May 3rd" note describes (roster additions, the Saturday Slamfest card, matches folded into the next Thursday Thrashin'). No comparable cluster of matching content exists near any other April 30 within the guestbook's own 1998–2000 span (its next entries jump to March 1999, discussing an unrelated European Title feud).

name: Thursday Thrashin' (April 30)
notes: A commentary-team-narrated results script; the only full RESULTED show the surviving record preserves (two further cards were announced but never resulted — see aew-saturday-slamfest-upcoming and aew-thursday-thrashin-upcoming, both results-free). Full match-by-match structuring was done for this one show given its small size; the rest of the corpus (roster/titles/stables snapshots) was not similarly structured. The rotating commentary team (Prez Ryan, Tony Shavoni, Vince MacMahon, Sting), ring announcer (Howard Finkel) and referee (Nick Patrick) are billed under real or original names throughout and are captured as angle appearances.
